summary: Placenta extracts (human placental extract preparations) are biogenic tissue extracts marketed mainly in India and parts of East Asia as topical (gel/solution) and injectable products promoted to aid wound healing, non-healing ulcers and granulation tissue formation, and, in injectable form, as an adjunct in conditions such as chronic pelvic inflammatory disease. The extracts contain a mixture of peptides, nucleotides, amino acids and other low-molecular-weight constituents and are proposed to have biogenic-stimulant, anti-inflammatory and tissue-regenerating actions, though high-quality controlled evidence for efficacy is limited. They are NOT FDA-approved as drugs; usage and dosing follow Indian manufacturer labelling and regional clinical practice. Because they are derived from human tissue, there is a theoretical concern about transmissible agents (manufacturers state viral inactivation/screening), and they should be avoided in pregnancy and in patients with known hypersensitivity. Their place in therapy is adjunctive and not supported by the strong evidence base of conventional wound-care measures.

moa: Placental extract preparations are complex biogenic mixtures of peptides, nucleotides, amino acids, enzymes and other low-molecular-weight factors. They are proposed to act as biogenic stimulants that enhance local microcirculation, fibroblast activity and granulation, with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects that may favour tissue repair. The precise mechanism is not well defined and the clinical effect is not established by robust controlled trials; any benefit is considered adjunctive.
